      <content name="altTitle"><span class="qt2">Malignant</span> <span class="qt0">mesothelioma</span></content>
      <content name="FullSummary"><p>The tissue that lines your lungs, stomach, heart, and other organs is called mesothelium. <span class="qt0">Mesothelioma</span>, also known as <span class="qt2">malignant</span> <span class="qt0">mesothelioma</span>, is cancer of that tissue. It usually starts in the lungs, but can also start in the abdomen or other organs. </p><p><span class="qt2">Malignant</span> <span class="qt0">mesothelioma</span> is rare but serious. Most people who get it have worked or lived in places where they inhaled or swallowed asbestos particles. After being exposed to asbestos, it usually takes a long time for the disease to form.</p><p>Symptoms include:</p><ul><li>Trouble breathing</li><li>Cough</li><li>Pain under the rib cage</li><li>Pain, swelling, or lumps in the abdomen</li><li>Weight loss for no known reason</li><li>Blood clots</li><li>Constipation</li><li>Fatigue</li></ul><p>Sometimes it is hard to tell the difference between <span class="qt2">malignant</span> <span class="qt0">mesothelioma</span> and lung cancer. To find out if you have <span class="qt0">mesothelioma</span>, your health care provider will likely use a physical exam, imaging tests, and a biopsy.</p><p><span class="qt2">Malignant</span> <span class="qt0">mesothelioma</span> is often found when it is advanced. This makes it harder to treat. Treatment options may include:</p><ul><li>Surgery</li><li>Radiation therapy</li><li>Chemotherapy</li><li>Immunotherapy</li><li>Targeted therapy, which uses drugs or other substances that attack specific cancer cells with less harm to normal cells</li></ul><p>NIH: National Cancer Institute</p></content>
